name: Russia

advisory.note: European governments advise against all or all but essential travel to Russia, citing the security situation, the risk of arbitrary detention, limited consular assistance and severely restricted flight and payment options. This page is a record of the European part of the country and is not a recommendation to travel there.

tagline: The European part alone is larger than any other country on the continent, and contains two of its greatest cities.
summary: Russia west of the Urals is geographically European and holds Moscow, St Petersburg and the Golden Ring of medieval towns. St Petersburg was built from nothing on a marsh in 1703 as a deliberate window on Europe, and the Hermitage is among the largest art collections in the world. This page records that; the advisory above governs whether any of it is currently reachable.

season.note: Historically the White Nights in June for St Petersburg. This is context, not a recommendation.

getting_around: Historically an extensive rail network including the overnight Moscow–St Petersburg services. Current air links to Europe are severely limited and Western cards do not work.
food: Blini, with sour cream and whatever is in season
Pelmeni and borscht, both contested across borders

festivals.name: Maslenitsa, the pancake week before Lent

know: Check your own government's current travel advice; most advise against travel.
This country is excluded from the Journey Planner.
Western bank cards do not function and consular assistance is limited.

regions.name: The Northwest
regions.summary: St Petersburg and the Baltic coast around it.

cities.name: Saint Petersburg
cities.summary: A planned imperial capital of canals and neoclassical facades, built on piles in a delta from 1703.
highlights: The Hermitage, in the Winter Palace
The Church of the Saviour on Spilled Blood and its mosaic interior
White Nights in June, when the bridges lift at night
Peterhof's fountains, which run without pumps

regions.name: Moscow & the Golden Ring
regions.summary: The capital and the medieval towns northeast of it.

cities.name: Moscow
cities.summary: A fortress, a cathedral square and a metro system built as underground palaces.
highlights: Metro stations with chandeliers and mosaics
The Tretyakov Gallery's icons, including Rublev's Trinity

timezone: MSK (UTC+3, no DST) in the European part
